extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and reportage guidance about censorship, what reporters should publish during wartime, and a numbered civil-defense preparedness checklist for New York State/City. Contains normative statements about when censorship is justified and operational criteria for emergency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censorship limited to military security
rubrics_metrics.description: “SECURITY” is the only reason for censorship; censorship must be restricted to matters of actual military security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece repeatedly asserts that while some censorship is necessary for the security of armed forces, censorship beyond that (political or image-protecting censorship) is unjustified. Example phrasing: '2. CENSORSHIP MUST BE RESTRICTED TO MATTERS OF ACTUAL MILITARY SECURITY.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish truthful reporting; public entitled to all news
rubrics_metrics.description: The American people are entitled to all the news, bad or good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorials and papers quoted argue newspapers should present facts honestly regardless of their impact on morale; reporters and editors should not withhold information merely because it is unfavorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not bar reporters who violated no security rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Banning newsmen who violated no 'security rules' is indefensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution from National Association of Radio News Directors and other press protests: reporters who are neither inaccurate nor in breach of security should not be excluded from reporting. Example case: Tom Lambert and Peter Kalischer were temporarily barred and later reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report exactly as seen, with common sense and regard for security
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents should 'tell the story ... exactly as they tell it ... without interference, and with no other censorship than their common sense and basic regard for military security.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters are urged to be factual and candid but to exercise common sense about revealing operational details that would harm military security. MacArthur’s overruling of field censorship is cited as restoring reporters' ability to report directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject political or image-protecting censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Political censorship (using security pretext to suppress political facts or to avoid embarrassing officials) is unacceptable and 'the worst' kind of censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: stories suppressed because they 'made the army look bad' or would 'irritate our allies' are characterized as politically motivated, depriving the public of vital information (e.g., Patton incident, stories stopped that compared Allied armies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Censor only to prevent aid/comfort to the enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Censorship is justified to deny military information to the enemy — i.e., to prevent giving 'aid and comfort' or disclosures that would help the enemy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is framed as the legitimate, narrowly circumscribed purpose of censoring dispatches from the front; anything beyond this rationale is questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-raid observation posts and filter centers (civil defense)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish air-raid observation posts (618 across the state) manned by volunteers and linked by telephone to flight-charting filter centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These posts' prime objective is to improve warning and to report to interceptor bases; staffing, telephone links and central filter centers are specified as necessary elements of an observation system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train specialists to treat atomic-bomb casualties
rubrics_metrics.description: State Health Department trains specialists in treating atom-bomb casualties (example: 93 specialists trained) and passes training to state nurses and private personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is to be cascaded to broader medical personnel (e.g., 15,000 private [nurses/medical workers]) within a stated timeframe (within the next two months in the article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan mass evacuation routes and logistics for major city
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a special plan to evacuate residents by rail, boat, bus and other means if conditions warrant; coordinate with transit officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evacuation planning should include logistical coordination among transit agencies and identification of routes and modes (rail, boat, bus, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: List hotels and accommodations for evacuees
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile a list of hotels and other accommodations statewide that can house evacuees from congested areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include lists of emergency hospitals and other facilities that could be used to receive evacuees and the wounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory construction equipment for emergency repair
rubrics_metrics.description: State Department of Public Works must inventory all state and privately-owned construction equipment for repair of roads, highways, rail and airport facilities and be ready for emergency mobilization within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inventory supports rapid repair and logistics after an attack; the requirement includes both public and private equipment and a clear mobilization timeframe (30 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish special defense communications network
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a special defense communications network using fire and police department radio/telephone systems and the city's radio station; assign a telephone company official full-time to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications resilience is a priority: integrate municipal radio/telephone assets and designate responsible personnel to manage the system full-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up detection teams for radioactive contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: City health department teams should be established for detection of radioactive-gassed areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detection capability is a direct preparedness metric; teams must be organized and trained to identify contaminated zones promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble food stockpile data and train inspectors for contamination risks
rubrics_metrics.description: State agriculture department should assemble data on cold-storage and warehouse food stockpiles and train field inspectors to detect possible contamination (chemical or bacteriological warfare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparedness includes knowing available food reserves and equipping inspectors with skills to detect contamination risks to food supplies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct test drills; validate plans by exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: No plan is good until it has been tried out — test drills are planned on various aspects of the civil defense program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational readiness must be validated through drills and exercises; plans should be adjusted based on drill outcomes.
